title: Token counters that aren't valid numbers, next to absent, null, zero and valid ones
matrix: input, output, cache-read and cache-write breakdowns
policy: P8: a counter is valid when it is a non-negative integral number below 2^53 (100.0, 5e1 and 1e2 are integers). Anything else (a string, a boolean, a fraction, a negative, a huge or non-finite number, an object or an array) is left out and flags the message as counted with an invalid counter; the message's valid counters still count. An absent or null counter reports nothing and isn't a flaw. Iterations follow the same rules, and a non-object iteration is skipped and flags the message.
derivation: a "100" -> input left out, [0, 50]. b true -> [0, 5]. c 1.5 -> [0, 2]. d null -> [0, 3], not a flaw. e explicit zeros -> [0, 0], 1 call. f 100.0 / 5e1 / 1e2 -> [100, 50, read 100]. g 1e30 -> [0, 7]. h 2^53 -> [0, 1]. i [10, 1] plus iteration claude-test-2 [20, output -4 left out] -> [20, 0, 1 call]; the element 42 is skipped. j cache_creation is a string -> the flat 30's tier is unknown (P9): [0, 1], 30 tier-unresolved. k object and array -> [0, 0]. l output -5 -> [40, 0]. claude-test-1: input 100+10+40 = 150, output 50+5+2+3+50+7+1+1+1 = 120, 30 tier-unresolved, read 100, 12 calls; claude-test-2 [20, 0, 1 call]. 150+120+30+100+20 = 420 tokens. Flawed: a b c g h i j k l = 9 messages; d e f are not. Today the string, object and array read as 0 too, but true reads as 1, 1.5 as 1, 1e30 and 2^53 as their integer values, and the negatives subtract.
